Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test failure in `testPcts()` relates to the method `getPct(Object)` in `Frequency` class, which is deprecated and implemented to call `getCumPct(Comparable<?>)` instead of `getPct(Comparable<?>)`. 

From the source code:
- `getPct(Object v)` (lines 301-304) is annotated with `@Deprecated` and returns `getCumPct((Comparable<?>) v)`.
- `getPct(Comparable<?> v)` (lines 315-322) returns the percentage of values equal to `v` by dividing the count of `v` by the total sum frequency.
- `getCumPct(Comparable<?> v)` (lines 490-496) returns the cumulative percentage up to `v` by dividing the cumulative frequency by the total sum frequency.

The bug report indicates that in version 2.0, `getPct(Object)` was changed to be implemented via `getCumPct` (cumulative percentage), whereas it was expected to behave like the old `getPct` (percentage for the exact value). This is an API breaking change causing the drop-in replacement problem when upgrading from version 1.2 to 2.0, as all calls to `getPct(Object)` now return cumulative percentages rather than simple percentages.

This also matches the observed test failure since the test checks the exact percentage of value 3 (using `getPct(Object)`), but the method returns a cumulative percentage instead because of the deprecated method implementation. The correct behavior should be to use the non-deprecated `getPct(Comparable<?>)` which computes the percentage of exact matches properly.

Hence, the root cause of the failure is that the deprecated method `getPct(Object)` incorrectly delegates to `getCumPct` instead of delegating to `getPct(Comparable<?>)`. This leads to wrong calculation and test failure. The test was probably using the deprecated signature (Object) and expecting the old behavior, which changed in this version. 

No relevant connections to unrelated recent bug reports are found, making the source of the fault clear in the current code and report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
